newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank shares end week up in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares end week up in Beirut.

text.p: Bank shares rose in the week ended on Friday on the Beirut Stock Exchange and Solidere shares were mixed while other stocks were completely inactive.
Banque Audi continued a price rally on high turnover reaching $17.00 from $16.5 last week. The share began trading at $15 on January 20.
"There is big volume sustaining the rise in Audi shares. There is still high demand on the share. I see it settling at around $18," a broker, who wished not to be identified, said.
Throughout the week, some 153,195 Audi shares were traded either on the BSE or in direct transactions outside the floor, making up 63 percent of the week's turnover in all listed stocks.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce also rose to $12.25 from $12 last Friday. The shares had first traded at $11.25 on December 30.
Solidere A shares -- distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district Solidere is rebuilding -- rose to $10.625 from $10.5.
B shares -- issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994 -- fell to $10.875 from $11.25 last Friday.
"There is nothing new pertaining to the Solidere shares. Intervention in the form of blocs of demand orders is keeping the prices at their current levels," the dealer said.
Total weekly turnover in all traded shares on the BSE floor was 376,559 shares from 495,153 last week. Total value of shares traded inside the hall was $4,684,173 from $5,979,464.
There was no trade in the four other firms listed on the BSE: Uniceramic, Eternit, Ciments Libanais and Ciments Blancs.
The BLOM stock index fell on the week by 0.84 percent to 911.69 while the LISPI share index rose 0.3 percent to 81.40.
